messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft DPA redline and sequencing for Medisuite - alignment request

Hi Anna,

Thanks for taking the time earlier in the week. Attached is Redwood's initial redline of the Data Processing Addendum (Medisuite_DPA_redline_v1.docx). We've focused edits on:
- clarifying controller/processor roles in Section 2,
- SCCs reference and execution path in Section 4, and
- the KMS/sous-proc encryption language in Section 7 to reflect Dedicated vs Hosted options.

Quick asks so we can sequence legal review:
1) Can your team confirm whether Medisuite will require the KMS clause to remain mandatory for Dedicated deployments?
2) Do you want the SCCs executed as a standalone exhibit or via DocuSign in the MSA sign flow?
3) Any local hosting constraints we should surface to Product/Infrastructure before we commit to the final language?

I propose a 30-minute alignment call on Tue/Wed next week to walk the redline and agree a small set of compromise edits (we'd like to finalize vendor-evidence alignment before legal kicks off procurement). If that works, send a couple slots and we'll lock it in.

Best,
Sean
Director, Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 2:45 PM Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@medisuite.com> wrote:
Sean — thanks for sending this over. We reviewed your redline with internal legal and our outside counsel (Mike Harrison). A few quick notes up front: 

- SCCs: we prefer SCCs executed as a standalone exhibit (our procurement system expects that), but we can accept DocuSign if Redwood's legal prefers a single-sign flow.
- KMS: our security team is hesitant to make KMS optional for Dedicated — they see it as a minimum control for PHI in our environment. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended fallback if KMS is not available in a given region?
- Processor roles: your edits tightened up the subprocessor approval flow which is good; however, we need primary/secondary processor clarity for our Data Protection Officer signoff.

Mike flagged two particular clauses and proposed alternate language (he's pasted suggested text below). We'll attach their write-up in a follow-up email. If Redwood can accept Mike's compromise on Section 7.2 (KMS exception path) and add a short SLA table for key rotation/retention, that will significantly shorten our internal clearance time.

We can do Wed Apr 21 at 10:00 AM CET for a call — does that work for your team?

Thanks,
Anna Lopez
Head of Legal Operations
Medisuite Health
anna.lopez@medisuite.com

---
Forwarded from Mike Harrison (Harrison & Cole LLP):
> Suggested language: 'Where KMS availability is constrained by hosting region, Redwood will implement equivalent encryption-in-transit and at-rest controls and provide written evidence of key custody procedures within 10 business days of request.'

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft DPA redline and sequencing for Medisuite - internal notes

Sean / Laura — quick internal notes after scanning Anna's reply and Mike's forwarded suggested language: 

- The KMS ask is tricky for some EU regions where we don't yet offer customer-managed KMS for Dedicated. We should be prepared to propose the 'equivalent controls + evidence' fallback they suggested; Security will need to validate the timeframe.
- Laura: can you loop in Product Security (Irene) and Ops to confirm whether a 10-business-day evidence window is operationally feasible?
- I'll start a short 'gap analysis' spreadsheet (internal-gap-analysis.xlsx) showing regions by capability (KMS yes/no, HSM availability, on-prem options). We can share that in the call to set expectations.

Also recommend we prepare two redline tracks for the meeting: (A) conservative (what legal prefers) and (B) pragmatic (what we can deliver quickly). Having both will help drive the negotiation.

Ben
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
Attachment: internal-gap-analysis.xlsx (internal)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Anna — thanks for the quick review and for sharing Mike's language. Wed Apr 21 10:00 AM CET works for us; we've booked a 30-minute slot. Calendar invite will come from our side in a moment.

Agreed next steps before the call: 
- Redwood to prepare two redline variants (Conservative / Pragmatic) and a 1-page capability matrix (Ben's gap analysis).
- Medisuite to confirm the SCCs signing preference (standalone exhibit vs DocuSign flow) and the internal DPO name for the call.
- Security alignment: Laura will bring Product Security and Ops onto the call to confirm operational feasibility of the 10-business-day evidence window.

If we reach a compromise on a short 'KMS exception' fallback language and a small SLA table for key rotation/retention, we expect legal signoff to clear procurement. After the call we'll consolidate agreed edits and aim to circulate a Final Redline v2 by EOD Apr 26 so procurement can start the signature path the following week.

Link to the working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-medidpa
DocuSign (if needed): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/RWD-2027-0345-signature-request

Thanks — see you on the call.

Sean
